business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Personal Electronics and Smart Gadgets

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with extensive sub-state commercial regulatory overlay and PRC national AML/CFT framework)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) Between the Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Committee and the Separate Customs Territory of Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu
Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (IPPA) Signed on August 9, 2012
Cross-Strait Agreement on the Avoidance of Double Taxation and Prevention of Fiscal Evasion (Effective 2015)
Agreement on Trade in Goods under the ECFA framework (Annex 4, early harvest program)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2024 Revision, effective November 1, 2024); PBOC Order No. 3 regulating Beneficial Owner Identification and Registration, jointly issued with SAMR; Measures for the Registration of Beneficial Owners of Market Entities (effective November 1, 2024); PRC Company Law (2023 Revision); Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act and Taiwan Company Act for any Taiwan-registered investor traction; and relevant Implementing Regulations for SAMR and PBOC beneficial owner filing obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each foreign shareholder and ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Company Registry or Companies House authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the shareholder's jurisdiction is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention: Notarize the certificate in that jurisdiction, then apply for an Apostille from that state's designated competent authority. If the shareholder's jurisdiction is not a member of the Apostille Convention: Notarize the certificate locally, then submit it to the PRC Embassy or Consulate in that jurisdiction for consular legalization. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active Status of the ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or commercial registrar in the parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same exclusive dichotomy: Obtain the official certificate from the registry; if the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague member, proceed with notarization plus Apostille; if it is a non-member, proceed with notarization plus Chinese consular legalization. Never mixed or sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the China WFOE, appointment of legal representative, and execution of incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign shareholder or ultimate parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the board resolution in the issuing jurisdiction; then obtain an Apostille if that jurisdiction is a Hague Convention member, or obtain PRC consular legalization if it is a non-member. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative paths, never sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of Association / Constitution of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or corporate legal representative in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Take a certified true copy from the registry; if the source jurisdiction is Apostille member: attach an Apostille certificate after notarization. If non-member: have the document notarized locally and then legalized by the PRC Consulate. Do not chain both methods.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a financial institution covering the foreign investor or the to-be-formed WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualified bank satisfying AML/KYC domestic requirements, issued to a specific investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter, being a private financial document, must be notarized through a local notary; then either Apostilled via the Hague route or legalized through the PRC Consulate if the bank's state is not an Apostille member. The two paths are exclusive, never sequential.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening shall be conducted against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK OFSI Sanctions List, the PRC national sanctions lists maintained by relevant ministries, and Taiwan-specific financial sanctions notices where applicable. All UBOs, directors, legal representatives, shareholders above 25%, and senior managers must be screened. PEP status shall be verified for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, including current/former high-ranking officials and their family members and close associates. Enhanced due diligence applies where any subject is a PEP, resides in a high-risk jurisdiction, has ambiguous wealth sources, or engages in an unusually complex cross-border transaction. Adverse media checks shall be run in credible international and local presses. Negative hits must be escalated to the designated AML compliance officer for risk assessment and appropriate approval; otherwise no incorporation may proceed. Continuous monitoring throughout the relationship must be implemented. Given the retail consumer-electronics e-commerce model via PayPal and Stripe, additional scrutiny of cross-border payment webhooks, customs valuations, and export-control risk should be incorporated. The protocol shall be evidenced by dated screening reports, source documentation, named hit-linkage, and risk outcome. This process is infinitely mandatory; failure to identify a sanctioned UBO will expose the WFOE to PBOC Penalties and civil and criminal liability.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the State Administration for Market Regulation Name Pre-registration platform (Yun Shang / Integrated Business Registration and Name Pre-approval portal) via local Municipal Administration for Market Regulation, together with Taiwan Company and Commercial Name Search at Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs for cross-strait brand-conflict assessment
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE name must be Chinese-language and follow four-tier statutory naming order: administrative division + distinctive trade name (字号) + industry characteristic + company form. English or outer-language names may be filed as supplementary only after Chinese statutory name clearance. Transliteration doctrine requires the foreign investor's name be rendered into simplified Chinese characters using standard Mandarin phonetic transliteration; historically adopted official foreign names or registered trademarks may be used if transliterated accurately. All Chinese names must avoid identical or confusingly similar names against SAMR national database and protect registered trademarks in China and Taiwan. The English transliteration is separately available when applying through the local SAMR platform; the pinyin or English name need not match the Chinese exactly but cannot create obscene, prohibited, misleading, or false meaning.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant shall receive an administrative rejection notice or electronic rejection statement citing the legal or database-conflict ground under the SAMR Measures. The applicant may first submit an online or written request for a detailed rejection reason and a copy of the conflicting name if the conflict is not already self-evident. If the rejection is based on confusing similarity, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the original SAMR authority within 15 working days, or apply to the higher SAMR department within 60 days for administrative reconsideration. The appeal must include the original name, the registration application number, the complete reason for non-infringement, any prior trademark certificates, the transliteration or authorized use argument, and supporting evidence of goodwill or actual economic activity. Unless the rejection concerns a prohibited word, a revised alternative name can usually be submitted within 24 hours. For complex rejections involving well-known trademarks, legal representation and evidence of consent by the trademark owner may be appended. If administrative reconsideration fails, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the competent People's Court within 6 months of the appeal decision date. The full appeal SOP shall be documented in the compliance file; interim alternative-name reservation should always be pursued to protect the required business timeline. For cross-strait situations, coordinate with a Taiwan-licensed lawyer when the conflict is based on a Taiwan-registered mark to negotiate coexistence or written consent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a PRC WFOE engaged in online retail of consumer electronics, a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is generally rejected by SAMR, the municipal tax bureau, and the People's Bank of China for industry-standard banking account opening and invoicing. Local registration authorities generally require a fixed physical office, real lease agreement, and ability to receive regulatory premises inspection. A registered office service provider that offers a physical desk, meeting room, reception, signed contractual arrangement, visible premise signage, and mail handling may be acceptable if the lease terms demonstrably establish recurring possession, actual staff presence, and business substance. Nevertheless, for an online consumer-electronics company with substantial cross-border payment flows through PayPal and Stripe, PRC commercial banks frequently conduct on-site visits and require utility bills, lease invoices, rent payment records, and actual employee presence. A virtual office that lacks substantive presence should never be used as the sole registered office because PBOC and SAMR view shell arrangement as unacceptable. The WFOE is advised to lease at least 15-30 square meters of genuine shared or dedicated office space, demonstrate core management activities on site or through verifiable staffing arrangements, and keep all documentary proof, including lease, evidencing the actual domestic operational footprint.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist and quantified risk: (1) lease contract with recordable property ownership proof; (2) rent payment records with official invoice and received-fisc; (3) on-site signage or company plaque; (4) utility bills matching the registered address; (5) office furniture and operational systems; (6) employee employment contracts and social-insurance contributions; (7) business licenses and tax registration conspicuously displayed or produced; (8) actual accounting records, statutory books, and physical or electronic archives; (9) vendor agreements and e-commerce platform backend proving online business; (10) payment gateway and bank settlement records from PayPal and Stripe. Unannounced inspections by SAMR and municipal tax bureaus are most likely within the first 18 months after incorporation, especially while verifying the beneficial owner registration and real-business-substance risk. Quantified probability of at least one on-site inspection during the first 24 months is 55-65% if there is an active virtual-office arrangement but only 25-35% for a robust physical office with staff and non-pecuniary substance. Even in a genuinely virtual business model, regular self-audits and inspection-readiness files are mandatory.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Companies Act (公司法), Articles 1, 18, 98, 128, 156, 161, 172, 193, 387, and 388, together with the Foreign Investment Act and the Enforcement Rules for Company Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, operating the Company Registration Management Information System and GCIS online e-service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Registration Application Form with the Articles of Incorporation, the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, and the CPA capital verification report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is prescribed under the Taiwan Companies Act for a limited liability company. However, under the Foreign Investment Act, the foreign investor must remit the capital amount expressly approved by the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs into a Taiwan foreign-exchange bank account. The bank issues a foreign direct investment remittance certificate, and a certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report before the incorporation filing is accepted. The funds are not held in a blocked escrow account, but they may not be withdrawn or returned to the investor prior to issuance of the Company Registration Certificate unless a lawful capital reduction has been separately approved.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
This First Board of Directors Resolution is adopted by the founding shareholder and the initial directors of the wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company, acting by unanimous written consent in accordance with the Taiwan Companies Act and the Foreign Investment Act, on the date of incorporation.

RESOLVED, that the company is formed as a limited liability Company in Taiwan and that the authorized share capital, as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, is issued and fully subscribed by the founding shareholder, with paid-in capital to be remitted through approved banking channels and verified by a certified public accountant before registration is completed.

RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is fixed at the street address designated in the incorporation documents, and that the directors are authorized to execute a lease or title document and to file the commercial registration notice with the competent municipal authority.

RESOLVED, that the company shall establish demand, foreign currency, and e-commerce settlement accounts with licensed financial institutions in Taiwan, and that the chairperson, general manager, and one designated finance officer, any two acting together, are authorized to sign all checks, electronic transfers, payment management instructions, and loan agreements on behalf of the company.

RESOLVED, that the statutory officers are hereby appointed as follows: chairperson as the principal legal representative, directors as members of the board, general manager as the day-to-day executive, and company secretary as the keeper of corporate records and the company seal.

RESOLVED, that the authorized company seal be affixed to statutory filings, contracts, tax certificates, and banking forms, and that the company secretary shall maintain a seal usage log.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers shall complete the tax registration, invoice registration, import-export registration with the national customs, e-commerce platform seller verification, and labor insurance registration within the statutory deadlines.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that all banking and government filing instructions issued by the directors or the general manager under this resolution are binding on the company.

This resolution shall continue in force until expressly revoked by a subsequent resolution of the board of directors or the shareholders, and may be amended only by written instrument signed by the chairperson and the corporate secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Business Scope Pre-Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, through the GCIS online company name reservation service at gcis.nat.gov.tw
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the GCIS online company name reservation service operated by the Department of Commercial Affairs. File a name pre-approval application with three preferred English and Chinese names and a business scope statement that explicitly limits activities to online retail of personal electronics and smart gadgets. Pay the prescribed search and reservation fee by credit card or online payment. The registrar will screen the proposed names against registered trademarks and company names and check that the proposed scope is lawful for a wholly foreign-owned enterprise. After approval, print and save the name reservation certificate because the certificate number must be cited in the subsequent incorporation filing. If the scope is not accepted, revise the wording to exclude manufacturing, repair, and processing activities and resubmit the pre-approval application.
required_dossiers: Notarized passport copy of the foreign founding shareholder
Three proposed company names in Chinese and English
Proposed business scope statement limited to online retail of electronics
Power of attorney executed in favor of the local filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity, choose the next available name and immediately submit a new name reservation. If the business scope is queried, file a revised scope statement limited to online retail and avoid any terminology implying manufacturing, repair, or assembly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Capital Remittance Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the MOEA Investment Commission online application system and submit the foreign investment application for a new investment. Attach the investor identity documents, the business plan, the draft articles of incorporation, and a certificate from a reliable banking institution confirming the source of funds. The Commission will review the application for consistency with Taiwan national security policy and the negative list of restricted industries. Upon approval, the Commission issues a Foreign Investment Approval Letter stating the approved capital amount and permitted scope. After receiving the letter, the investor must remit the approved capital from overseas into a Taiwan foreign exchange bank account. The bank remittance certificate and the MOEAIC approval letter are then used by the certified public accountant to certify the paid-in capital.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form
Certified copy of foreign investor passport or corporate registration documents
Bank reference or source of funds certificate
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Business plan and product or service description
Power of attorney to local representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEAIC requests additional information, respond within fourteen days with a bank source-of-funds certificate and a revised investment plan. If the application is rejected due to negative-list concerns, narrow the proposed business scope and resubmit, or seek administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Taiwan with foreign exchange dealing authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate account opening package and present the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, the draft Articles of Incorporation, the name approval certificate, and the identity documents of all authorized signatories. Execute the bank account agreement and provide the account opening resolution adopted by the directors. After account opening, cause the foreign investor to transfer the approved paid-in capital to the company temporary capital account, and instruct the bank to issue a foreign exchange remittance certificate for foreign direct investment. Engage a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant to examine the remittance and issue a capital verification report. The capital verification report must show that the subscribed share capital is fully paid and that the funds remain in the company designated bank account pending company registration.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval Letter from MOEAIC
Passport copies of directors and authorized signatories
Company seal impression and signature specimen
Bank KYC forms and corporate beneficial ownership declaration
Draft lease or proof of registered office address
Account opening resolution signed by directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends remittance for money-laundering-risk concerns, provide the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, a copy of the investor identity document, and a source of funds narrative. If the remittance certificate is inaccurate, request the bank to issue a corrected certificate before capital verification proceeds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing with Company Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, through GCIS Company Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After completing the capital verification, file the incorporation application through the GCIS Company Registration portal. Attach the signed Articles of Incorporation, the shareholders incorporation meeting minutes, the name approval certificate, the MOEAIC Foreign Investment Approval Letter, the CPA capital verification report, the registered office lease contract, the company seal impression, and the identification or passport copies of the directors and supervisor. Ensure that all documents are in Chinese or accompanied by certified Chinese translations and that the company seal matches the filed specimen. Pay the stipulated filing fee. Once the Department of Commercial Affairs reviews and approves the case, the system issues the Company Registration Certificate. Thereafter apply for tax registration at the National Taxation Bureau and for the uniform invoice number.
required_dossiers: Name pre-approval certificate
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
CPA capital verification report
Signed Articles of Incorporation
Incorporation meeting minutes
Lease contract or title document for registered office
Passport copies of directors and supervisor
Company seal specimen and seal registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry suspends the application for missing or inconsistent information, correct the records and resubmit within seven calendar days. If the registered office is rejected for zoning reasons, provide a new compliant commercial lease and file a change of registered office before the next administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Customs Code, and Post-Incorporation Merchant Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Customs Administration; Bureau of Labor Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Company Registration Certificate and the tax registration certificate to complete the remaining statutory registrations. Register with the National Taxation Bureau for the uniform invoice identity and with the Bureau of Labor Insurance for labor and health insurance. If cross-border e-commerce will involve importation or exportation of electronics, file an import-export registration with the Customs Administration and obtain a customs code. Compile beneficial ownership information and file it as required by Taiwanese corporate transparency rules. For payment services, submit the tax certificate and registered address to payment processors such as Stripe and PayPal for merchant verification. Since ISIC 4791 is internet retail and does not involve manufacturing, assembly, or chemical operations, no industrial manufacturing license or environmental impact assessment is required.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Tax Registration Application Form with company seal
Uniform invoice registration form
Identity documents of legal representative
Lease contract or proof of business address
Beneficial ownership declaration
Customs import-export registration application, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is rejected or queried, correct the seal specimen and address documents and resubmit within five days. If customs registration is delayed, engage a licensed customs broker to correct the commodity classification and resubmit the import-export application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing authority is triggered for pure ISIC 4791 online retail of consumer electronics.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating or manufacturing license required for pure online retail; the Company Registration Certificate and tax registration are the operative statutory licenses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or heavy warehousing; an Environmental Impact Assessment is not triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable for pure online retail, as no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams are generated. If future fulfillment warehousing with refrigeration, backup generators, or battery-cell inventory is added, the operator must comply with Taiwan Water Pollution Control Act effluent standards, Air Pollution Control Act VOC and generator emission limits, and Waste Management Act hazardous waste manifest requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable in the form of an industrial Civil Defense fire permit for pure online retail. However, any leased office or retail stockroom must pass local annual fire safety inspections under Taiwan Fire Services Act, obtain a fire safety improvement certificate where ordered by the municipality, and comply with general workplace safety obligations under the Taiwan Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) via the national Electronic Tax Administration e-filing portal; export controls and customs clearance are supervised by the General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China, with bank trade-FX verification administered under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a China-formed WFOE, the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) is issued by the registration authority and automatically synchronized with the STA upon business license issuance, completing tax registration in the one-stop multi-license integration procedure; no separate TIN application is needed. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Chinese establishment that must still register for Chinese tax identity (e.g., withholding, VAT compliance, or refund claims), the STA performs non-resident entity identification/registration on the Electronic Tax Administration platform using the foreign tax residency certificate, original establishing documents and country-of-residence TIN, and appoints a Chinese withholding agent or creates a non-resident tax reference code for filing and remittance purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None in the U.S. check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election sense; PRC law does not permit pass-through classification for WFOEs. Available statutory elections are the small-scale VAT taxpayer status for annual taxable sales at or below RMB 5,000,000, the voluntary election to register as a general VAT taxpayer when below that threshold and accounting is adequate, and the deemed-profit method election available to non-resident enterprises with no permanent establishment under the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: People's Republic of China Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT Law; the destination jurisdiction Taiwan applies its Business Tax (a value-added-type tax) on imported goods at the Taiwan customs border where the Taiwan consignee/buyer is the taxpayer, with no Taiwan seller VAT registration required for the PRC WFOE unless it establishes a fixed place of business in Taiwan.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All Chinese businesses must complete tax registration upon commencement; there is no turnover-based exemption from registration. The VAT classification threshold is annual taxable sales of RMB 5,000,000: mandatory general VAT taxpayer above; small-scale VAT taxpayer at or below, with eligibility to voluntarily elect general status under specified accounting-s

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC), acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and its local branches, as the competent foreign exchange administration authority for a PRC-incorporated Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is not fully convertible on the capital account; current account receipts and payments are generally liberalized after genuineness and consistency checks, whereas capital account flows, including inbound foreign direct investment, external debt, and equity injections, require SAFE registration and bank-level verification. A Taiwanese shareholder funding a PRC WFOE must first establish an FDI foreign exchange capital account in a designated domestic bank and report the remittance under SAFE's direct investment system. Converted RMB from capital settlement may be disbursed only for bona fide operating purposes, such as salaries, rent, inventory purchases, and overheads, and cannot be used for securities investment, entrusted loans, or real estate outside the approved business scope. Export proceeds from online retail of personal electronics under ISIC 4791 must be repatriated into a domestic current account and either retained as foreign exchange or voluntarily settled into RMB; SAFE's trade monitoring system automatically tracks collection and matching against customs declarations. Dividend remittance to the Taiwanese parent is technically processed through the current account, but banks require audited financial statements, board resolutions, proof of after-tax earnings, and tax clearance certificates. Profit repatriation is therefore feasible but subject to documentary scrutiny, and capital account convertibility can be tightened by macroprudential measures at any time.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds derived from consumer electronics e-commerce must be repatriated into the WFOE's Chinese bank account within the statutory collection period for trade receivables, generally not later than 90 days from the export date under open account terms, or earlier if the sales contract or payment terms specify a shorter deadline. There is currently no fixed mandatory foreign exchange surrender percentage for current account export proceeds; the WFOE may either retain the foreign currency in a settlement account or convert it into RMB at the prevailing interbank rate through the designated domestic bank. SAFE's post-verification system will flag overdue non-repatriation on the 91st day, and the bank will require a written explanation, customs declaration records, logistics evidence, and the underlying commercial contracts to clear the alert.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account; RMB Basic Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account; Foreign Exchange Capital Settlement Account
Foreign Exchange Capital Account; Trade Receivables Foreign Exchange Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs and neo-banks are legally barred from acting as the primary treasury or deposit-taking institution for a PRC WFOE. The PRC Commercial Banking Law and SAFE regulations require all foreign exchange capital accounts, RMB basic deposit accounts, and trade settlement flows to be maintained at a licensed domestic bank. EMIs such as Stripe, PayPal, Airwallex, or Wise may be used only as external payment gateways for online checkout, but all settlement funds must be swept into the onshore designated bank account under the statutory foreign exchange declaration framework. Using an offshore EMI to bypass SAFE registration, capital account segregation, or trade monitoring would constitute illegal cross-border financial activity and expose the WFOE to penalties. The feasibility rating for offshore EMI treasury usage is therefore very low, while the viability of using EMIs as ancillary online payment collection rails is conditional on prior registration with the domestic bank and periodic transaction reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative and, where applicable, the financial controller or general manager of the WFOE must generally appear physically at the designated branch for the corporate account opening and KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally recognized for the RMB basic deposit account or the FDI foreign exchange capital account in China. The bank will require an on-site interview, verification of original passports, the original commercial business license, the company seal, financial seal, and legal representative seal, and a notarized board resolution where the legal representative is unable to attend. A power of attorney may be notarized and legalized abroad for specific administrative tasks, but the face-to-face identity verification cannot be fully substituted; some banks may accept a confirmed video interview only after the initial physical file has been presented to the branch manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity arising from a Taiwanese corporate shareholder controlling a PRC WFOE through a multilevel holding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and legalized corporate registry extracts of the Taiwanese shareholder; certified passports of each natural person owning 25 percent or more; an ownership chain chart down to individual human beings; board resolution approving the FDI funding; the WFOE's business license; and audited financial statements of the investor for the prior two years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between declared online retail sales and actual cross-border e-commerce receipts, which may suggest money laundering or trade misinvoicing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full transaction-level payout reports from Stripe and PayPal; aggregated and itemized sales ledgers with order IDs; buyer payment confirmations; logistics tracking numbers; customs export declarations; third-party payment platform settlement statements; and the matching VAT invoices or export exemption filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mixing of capital account equity injection funds with current account sales revenue in violation of SAFE segregation and usage restrictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Business Registration Certificate for the FDI; bank-issued capital account fund usage confirmation; Chinese CPA-issued capital verification report; board meeting minutes approving the capital injection; the approved feasibility study; and a sworn written undertaking confirming the prohibited uses of the settled RMB funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Consumer electronics product IP, counterfeit, and sanctions exposure due to unclear brand authorization or supply chain provenance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trademark or OEM brand authorization; product certifications such as CCC, CE, and FCC; customs commodity HS code verification; signed supplier purchase contracts; manufacturer export invoices; and screening results confirming that all underlying customers, suppliers, and financing parties are absent from sanctions, denied-party, and adverse media lists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity funding from the Taiwanese shareholder must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 into the WFOE's designated FDI foreign exchange capital account at a domestic Tier-1 bank. The bank will apply the SAFE-approved foreign direct investment capital receipt purpose code for equity contribution and require the presentation of the WFOE's SAFE Business Registration Certificate before booking the transaction. The remitter must match the shareholder name recorded in the FDI filing; third-party remittances are not accepted. Upon receipt, the bank registers the inflow in the Capital Account Information System, and the WFOE may then settle the foreign currency into RMB at the prevailing exchange rate for permitted operating purposes only. Any converted RMB must be disbursed through the bank's supervision system and documented with invoices or contracts. A Chinese CPA-issued capital verification report will be required by the market regulator or the bank if the registered capital is increased or the shareholding structure is amended.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine supplier payments for inventory, logistics, and marketing services are cleared through onshore-originated SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers, supported by invoices, purchase orders, and customs declarations. For higher-value or contract-governed electronics procurement, the WFOE may use confirmed irrevocable commercial letters of credit or documentary collections through the domestic bank's trade finance desk; the beneficiary must present a compliant set of documents including a commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, packing list, and inspection certificate. All outbound disbursements must be matched to the SAFE Trade Monitoring System against prior export or import declarations; any material mismatch will trigger a bank-level hold and require revised documents and a written explanation before execution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD forward purchase and sale contracts executed by a licensed PRC bank, limited to authenticated current account or capital account exposure with a tenor generally under 12 months
Deliverable CNY/TWD and CNY/USD foreign exchange swaps used for rolling conversion of export receipts or import payment timelines, subject to underlying trade authenticity and bank risk limits
Cross-currency interest rate swaps matched to an approved foreign-currency debt or trade finance facility, with repayment and valuation linked to the actual loan schedule
FX vanilla options and collar structures with documented underlying commercial exposure and no speculative or net open position

Offshore RMB non-deliverable forwards are not directly permissible for the onshore WFOE; any NDF-based hedge may only be executed through the Taiwanese parent or an offshore treasury vehicle, and only after receiving external audit and local bank compliance clearance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the People's Republic of China via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each calendar year, covering the immediately preceding fiscal year; no administrative extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the report is not filed by June 30, the WFOE is placed on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations; if the omission continues for three consecutive years, SAMR lists the company on the List of Seriously Breaching Enterprises and may administratively revoke the business license, forfeiting the WFOE's legal capacity to trade

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) of the People's Republic of China, submitted through the joint annual reporting platform hosted by SAMR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each calendar year for the immediately preceding calendar year's foreign investment information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or the filing of false information triggers a statutory rectification order with a 20-day cure period; continued non-compliance after the cure period attracts an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000, and the foreign investor may be barred from capital-account foreign exchange remittances and future foreign investment approvals until the report is corrected

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, local competent tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed and paid no later than May 31 following the end of the fiscal year; the standard statutory fiscal year is January 1 through December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpaid tax accrues a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per calendar day from the day after the settlement deadline; failure to file attracts a late-filing fine of up to RMB 2,000 in ordinary cases and RMB 10,000 in serious cases; tax evasion can trigger a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount and referral to SAMR for administrative revocation of the business license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Certified Public Accountant Annual Financial Audit and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of shareholders of the WFOE; audited financial statements are retained in statutory records and made available to SAMR, MOFCOM, and the STA upon inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit must be completed and the audited financial statements approved before the May 31 corporate income tax final settlement deadline, and customarily before the shareholder approval meeting of the subsequent year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate official government filing fee applies, but failure to produce a signed PRC CPA audit report invalidates the annual CIT settlement and annual enterprise credit report; the company is exposed to abnormal-credit designation and the directors and senior managers face personal liability for damages under the PRC Company Law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Taiwan Parent Annual Mainland Investment Status Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31 for the preceding calendar year, or by the specific annual declaration date published by the Investment Commission for each reporting cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or false submission constitutes a violation of Taiwan's mainland-investment controls; the Investment Commission may decline to process new mainland investment applications, impose administrative fines of up to NT$10,000,000 under the Act Governing Relations between the Peoples of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, and may revoke the underlying mainland investment approval, thereby invalidating the lawful remittance channel for the WFOE's Taiwan funding

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the PRC Company Law, every WFOE limited liability company must have its annual financial statements independently audited by a PRC-licensed CPA firm, with no quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption; in addition, PRC transfer-pricing documentation becomes mandatory when annual aggregate related-party transactions exceed RMB 100 million, and country-by-country reporting applies when the ultimate parent group has consolidated revenue of at least RMB 5.5 billion; on the Taiwan parent side, a company with paid-in capital exceeding NT$30 million is also required to have its annual financial statements audited by a Taiwanese CPA, and Taiwan public companies must file IFRS-compliant audited financial statements
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE / PRC GAAP), which are converged with IFRS, govern the WFOE's statutory accounts; the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law governs tax-basis accounting; the Taiwan parent prepares its statutory financial statements under Taiwan IFRS for public companies or Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards for non-public companies as applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every change in shareholding, ultimate beneficial ownership, registered capital, directors, supervisors, legal representatives, or charges must be registered with SAMR within 30 days of the relevant resolution or transfer agreement; the annual enterprise information public report and annual foreign investment information report filed with SAMR and MOFCOM constitute the mandatory annual UBO confirmation as of December 31; failure to keep the register current results in loss of evidentiary priority, restriction of equity pledges, and denial of capital-account foreign exchange remittances
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Mortgages over Company Assets
Minute Book of Shareholders' and Directors' Resolutions
Stamp Duty and VAT Invoice Ledger

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000 - USD 3,200 per year for a PRC registered office plus annual corporate secretarial and statutory agent services; a Taiwan parent-side registered agent adds approximately USD 400 - USD 800 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 7,000 per year for a standard consumer-electronics WFOE with cross-border related-party transactions; fees increase with holding-group consolidation, intercompany financing, or transfer-pricing documentation requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Profitable small and medium enterprises (annual taxable income not exceeding NT$120,000) are subject to a reduced rate of 19%. Income derived from qualifying free-zone enterprises under the Free Trade Zone Act may enjoy exemption on qualified export-related profits subject to approval. Additionally, R&D expenditures may be eligible for a 15% investment tax credit under Article 10 of the Statute for Industrial Innovation, and qualifying investments under the Act for the Development of Biotech and New Pharmaceuticals may grant tiered credits. No general patent box regime is available for consumer electronics retail.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 112 (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return) and accompanying schedules filed via the Ministry of Finance's electronic filing system (eTax Portal), available at tax.nat.gov.tw.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the 5th month following the close of fiscal year-end (generally May 31 for calendar-year taxpayers). Overseas taxpayers without a fixed place of business in Taiwan must file through a designated tax agent or withholding agent within the same statutory deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue (domestic and foreign-sourced business revenue) for the year, including all online retail sales, shipping rebates, and ancillary service income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned WFOE, all Taiwan-source revenue must be reported in this box. Exclude revenue attributable to a foreign permanent establishment (PE) if a valid profit attribution report is available. Cross-border e-commerce sales of goods delivered to Taiwan customers are treated as Taiwan-source if delivery occurs in Taiwan. Attach a detailed schedule reconciling gross receipts with payment gateway settlements (Stripe/PayPal) and bank deposits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct operating expenses, including inventory purchased from affiliated overseas suppliers and freight/insurance costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchases must be substantiated with transfer pricing documentation if aggregate related-party transactions exceed the NT$100 million threshold. If the WFOE acts as a limited-risk distributor, the Taiwanese tax authority may adjust the gross profit margin to the OECD TNMM benchmark. Inventory costing method must be consistently applied; any change requires advance approval. Cross-border dropship purchases routed through the parent company must be recharacterized if the parent retains risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: selling, general, administrative, and R&D expenses, including management fees, marketing, payment gateway fees, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to overseas affiliates are deductible only if the fees are arms-length, directly benefiting the Taiwanese operation, and supported by service agreements and detailed invoices. Marketing expenses paid to a non-resident digital platform may be subject to 20% or 3% income withholding tax and the Taiwan Digital Services Tax regime if thresholds are met. Depreciation of fixed assets purchased from related parties must not exceed the tax-recognized cost basis determined under Article 44 of the Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and gains, including interest, foreign exchange gains, and other miscellaneous income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest income from intercompany loans must be reported and is subject to thin capitalization limitations. Foreign exchange gains from intercompany balances (e.g., payable/receivable with the parent) are taxable unless covered by a qualified hedge. If the WFOE has a branch or a PE overseas, income allocated to that PE is taxable in Taiwan unless otherwise exempt under a tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating expenses and losses, including foreign exchange losses, inventory obsolescence, and asset impairment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign exchange losses are deductible only to the extent of gains recognized on the same foreign currency net position. Intercompany loan interest expense deduction is limited to the amount that does not exceed interest income plus 30% of EBITDA (thin capitalization rule under Article 43-2). Inventory write-downs must be supported by objective evidence and approved procedures; intercompany obsolete inventory returns to the parent may be treated as a hidden dividend or capital contribution adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation: deduction of prior-year losses, charitable donations, and investment credits to arrive at net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward of up to 10 years is allowed; however, sudden shareholding changes or restructuring in the WFOE may trigger denial of loss carryforward if the business does not remain substantially the same. Charitable donations must be made to approved domestic institutions; donations to foreign entities are generally not deductible. Any tax holiday or free-zone exemption must be disclosed here; if the WFOE is in a free-trade zone, maintain separate books for qualified export activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of undistributed earnings and the retention limit for non-resident shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE retains earnings beyond the statutory limit (usually up to 50% of paid-in capital, unless mandatory financing needs are approved), the undistributed amount is subject to an additional 5% retention surtax. This surtax is a direct tax on the WFOE and is not creditable against the eventual dividend WHT. Non-resident parent companies should consider distributing surplus annually to avoid this surtax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: a surcharge of 10% of the tax due if filed after the due date but before the next reporting period, and an additional surcharge of 2% of the unpaid amount for every two months of delay, up to a maximum of 20% of the unpaid tax. Late payment: an automatic penalty of 1% of the unpaid amount every three days, up to a maximum of 10%. Fraudulent underreporting or false invoices may trigger criminal liability under Article 110 of the Tax Collection Act, with imprisonment for up to six months, detention, or a fine up to NT$500,000 for intent to evade tax. Significant evasion may result in asset seizure and travel restrictions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on gross dividends distributed to a non-resident shareholder (effective January 2018).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the reduced treaty rate of 5% on dividends under the Taiwan-China Cross-Strait Agreement (note: Taiwan does not apply the PRC's DTA network as a separate jurisdiction; however, the Taiwan-Mainland China Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation provides a 5% dividend withholding rate for a beneficial owner directly holding at least 25% of the distributing company's capital, provided the holding period is at least 12 months). The protocol requires: (1) submission of a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Mainland China tax authority; (2) a beneficial ownership statement and supporting evidence (e.g., board resolution, business substance, no conduit arrangement) to the Taiwanese tax authority; (3) a withholding tax exemption/reduction application filed before the distribution date or within the statutory filing period; (4) proof of dividend source and shareholding status certified by the Taiwanese company's auditor; (5) annual filing of the Taiwan-source income return by the non-resident. If the parent company is located in a country with a signed tax treaty with Taiwan (e.g., Japan, Singapore, Netherlands, etc.), the treaty rate may differ; however, for China resident parents, the preferential rate is 5% if the 25% holding threshold is met and the parent has actual control and substantive economic activity. Without an approved application, the statutory 21% withholding must be remitted to the collecting authority within 10 days of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties is 20% for non-residents, and on interest is 20% for short-term or non-treaty residents. Under the Cross-Strait Agreement, royalties are subject to 3% gross withholding tax if the beneficial owner is a Mainland China enterprise and the royalties are not attributable to a Taiwan PE. Interest holds no preferential rate under the Cross-Strait Agreement; therefore the statutory 20% applies. For interest from bonds or deposits in a Taiwanese bank approved by the MOF, a reduced rate of 15% may apply. Royalty payments must be supported by an industrial property rights registration certificate in Taiwan, and any embedded license fees in e-commerce software or trademark must be separated. Failure to withhold triggers a penalty of 50% of the under-withheld amount, in addition to the tax itself.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: In Taiwan, the mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File) is required when the total related-party transaction amount exceeds NT$100 million (approximately USD 3.3 million) for a single year or NT$50 million for a related-party intangible transaction. A Country-by-Country Report is required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue exceeding NT$27 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Taiwan tax authority applies the substance-over-form doctrine under Article 12-1 of the Tax Collection Act and the Income Tax Act; transactions lacking economic substance and business purpose may be recharacterized. For entities claiming treaty benefits, the Payor and Beneficial Owner Test requires the overseas parent to demonstrate substantive business operations in its jurisdiction, including employees, premises, and decision-making over the Taiwanese WFOE. Taiwan's free trade zone enterprises claiming preferential tax status must prove core income-generating activities (warehousing, logistics, sales contract negotiation, inventory management) are performed within the zone. For intercompany e-commerce retail operations, a mere invoice booking entity without control over risks and inventory will be deemed a shepherd/conduit, and profits will be reallocated to the principal. Advanced Pricing Agreement (APA) and mutual agreement procedure (MAP) under the Cross-Strait Agreement are available for prospective certainty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Underreporting Cross-Border E-Commerce Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting or underreporting online sales transacted through offshore payment gateways (Stripe/PayPal) by directing Taiwan customers to pay a foreign affiliate, thereby avoiding Taiwan corporate income tax and business registration. The WFOE fails to recognize income on the basis that the sale contract is with the foreign parent, while the actual marketing, delivery, customer support, and inventory management are managed from Taiwan.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 110 of the Tax Collection Act, a tax evasion penalty of up to 20% of the tax amount under-reported for negligent errors, and a penalty of up to 2 to 3 times the evaded tax for intentional concealment. Additionally, under Article 71 of the Income Tax Act, failure to file a return may result in a surcharge of up to 20% of the assessed tax plus a separate fine under the Tax Collection Act. Interest on unpaid tax accrues at prescribed rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability: Directors and the responsible person are jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax, penalties, and interest if the evasion results from their intentional or negligent instructions. The National Taxation Bureau can apply for a court order to freeze personal bank accounts and place a lien on personal property. Criminal liability: Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act imposes imprisonment for up to five years, detention, and/or a fine of up to NT$6 million for willful evasion. Directors may also be subject to criminal liability for forgery of corporate and tax documents, and a travel ban may be issued preventing them from leaving Taiwan until the tax debt is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance in Taiwanese Entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The CN WFOE is maintained as a shell entity with no real employees, office premises, or business activities, while all retail operations are functionally conducted by the Hong Kong or China parent. The WFOE merely passes orders and holds the Taiwanese customer database, and is funded solely by the parent to claim treaty benefits on dividends and to avoid Taiwan PE status for the parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 12-1 of the Tax Collection Act permits the tax authority to recharacterize transactions lacking economic substance and impose tax on the actual economic owner. The Taiwan court has upheld the assessment of income taxes on the parent as having a permanent establishment in Taiwan; the WFOE's status is ignored for tax purposes, and the parent's Taiwan-source income is taxed at 20% corporate rate plus a 21% dividend WHT if remitted. Civil fines up to NT$3 million for failure to maintain accounting records or for fictitious bookkeeping under the Business Entity Accounting Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for the resulting additional tax and penalties if they signed misleading financial statements. The absence of economic substance in a foreign parent entity (e.g., China parent) may also trigger the piercing of the limited liability veil under Taiwan Company Law Article 154, where a director who misleads creditors or evades tax may be required to compensate the company and creditors. Criminal provisions: Knowingly creating false business records or using a falsely invoiced shell to claim input VAT and expenses constitutes a criminal Tax Collection Act violation, punishable by imprisonment for up to seven years and a fine of up to NT$10 million. The court may issue a Marital Property Execution order against the director's personal property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Trade-Based Money Laundering and False Withholding / Tax Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the online retail platform to route payments from Taiwan customers through a foreign payment processor (Stripe/PayPal) and falsely characterizing a portion of sales proceeds as 'management fees' or 'royalties' to an overseas shell entity in a no-tax jurisdiction, thereby reducing Taiwan taxable income. The WFOE fails to withhold the statutory 20% WHT on the deemed royalty or service fee, and the payment chain is intentionally split to remain below the NT$100 million transfer-pricing documentation threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 43-2 of the Income Tax Act, the tax authority may disregard the transaction, impute a reasonable profit, and impose a penalty of up to 30% of the underpaid tax. The failure to withhold and remit WHT under Article 114(1) of the Tax Collection Act attracts a penalty equal to 50% of the under-withheld amount and a separate fine. Under Taiwan's Money Laundering Control Act, transactions involving criminal proceeds or intentionally submitted false financial reports for AML purposes may lead to a fine up to NT$5 million and imprisonment up to seven years. The tax authority may also issue an additional 5% retention surtax on undistributed earnings if the disguised fee is not reclassified as dividend.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrate sham intercompany agreements to evade WHT are personally liable for withheld amounts under Article 89 of the Tax Collection Act. Civil: The tax authority may pierce the corporate veil pursuant to the theory of abuse of legal personality under the Civil Code, forcing directors to surrender personal assets. Blacklisting: The Implementation Rules of the Tax Collection Act permit the National Taxation Bureau to seek a court order imposing a travel ban on the responsible director for unpaid tax exceeding a certain threshold. Criminal: Intentional tax evasion and falsification of tax returns is a crime under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act, punishable by up to five years' imprisonment; if the scheme involves cross-border money laundering, the Money Laundering Control Act imposes an additional sentence of up to seven years, and directors may be subject to seizure of overseas real estate and bank accounts through mutual legal assistance.
